prerequisites: Knowledge in mechanics, machine elements, and fluid mechanics are advantageous.

learning_outcomes.text: Define and apply modern strategies, methods, and measures in lightweight construction.
Explain sandwich structures in terms of their construction, functionality, and manufacturing technologies.
Explain the use of sandwich and composite structures in aircraft components, as well as the effects of mass reductions on performance, emissions, and costs.
Understand the fundamentals of aerodynamics and explain important aerodynamic concepts and relationships.
Compare propulsion types and identify and evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of different propulsion types.
Understand the efficient energy conversion in engines at high speeds and the bridging of speed differences to the rotors using gears.
Analyze the performance of airfoils and propellers.
Estimate and evaluate the flight duration and range of model gliders.
Conduct, evaluate, and interpret results from experiments on lightweight structures in relation to theoretical models.
Develop problem-solving and transfer skills by comparing findings from theory and experiment.
Collaborate effectively in teams, discuss different perspectives, and jointly develop solutions.

syllabus_topics: Strategies, measures, and methods in lightweight construction
Comparisons of structural and mass properties with alternative lightweight construction approaches
Introduction to the technology and theory of sandwich structures
Application of sandwich structures in aircraft and their components
Practical experimental investigations with sandwich components
Effects of structural mass on fuel consumption, CO2 emissions, and operating costs of aircraft
Aerodynamic forces and coefficients: lift and drag and their dependence on angle of attack. Lift polar and drag polar. Aerodynamic limits: stall.
Calculation of airfoil shapes and aerodynamic properties.
Wing aerodynamics, lift and induced drag.
Flow visualization of a model wing with smoke in the wind tunnel.
Gliding performance: longitudinal equations of motion, flight duration and range.
Associated laboratory exercise: competition for designing/building/flying model gliders.
Demonstration of the effects of propeller parameters such as blade pitch and rotor diameter on thrust.
Introduction to the fundamentals of aviation gears.
